jobs.occupation: Senior Scientist, Upstream, Late-Stage Process Development
jobs.description:
**Are you an experienced upstream scientist who enjoys solving complex process challenges and turning scientific data into clear recommendations? Do you enjoy leading late-stage development studies and using your expertise to help clients move their processes towards clinical and commercial manufacturing?

**At AGC Biologics in Søborg, we are looking for a Senior Scientist to join our Late-Stage Process Development team.

You will join a multidisciplinary team of six scientists and eight technicians working across upstream, downstream, and analytical disciplines. Together, we develop and characterize robust mammalian cell culture processes supporting clinical and commercial manufacturing.

**About The Job

**As a Senior Scientist, you will lead upstream late-stage development activities, with a particular focus on process characterization, down-scale model qualification, and scientific data analysis.

You will be responsible for your assigned scientific activities, from study design and data interpretation to technical recommendations and reporting. As a subject matter expert (SME), you will also serve as a key scientific contact for clients and internal stakeholders, helping explain process performance, address technical challenges, and recommend practical next steps.

**Your Main Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Planning and leading process characterization (PC) studies, including experimental design, data evaluation, and preparation of PC work reports.

• Designing and evaluating down-scale model qualification (DSMQ) studies to demonstrate representativeness of manufacturing-scale processes.

• Applying statistical methods, including Design of Experiments (DoE), and tools such as JMP to support data-driven scientific conclusions.

• Contributing to FMECA and other process risk assessments to identify critical process parameters and support control strategy development.

• Supporting late-stage development activities, including Limit of In Vitro Cell Age (LIVCA) studies, Working Cell Bank (WCB) activities, scale-up, and technology transfer.

• Providing scientific guidance to laboratory technicians, collaborating across functions, and communicating technical findings, project status, and recommendations to clients.

You will also contribute to technical documentation, including development reports, technology transfer documentation, and relevant regulatory submissions.

**Who Are We Looking For?

**We are looking for an experienced scientist with strong technical knowledge of mammalian upstream processes and the ability to translate scientific data into practical recommendations.

**We Imagine That You

**

• Hold a Bachelor's, Master's, or PhD degree in biotechnology, biochemical engineering, or another relevant scientific discipline.

• Have at least five years of relevant industry experience with a Master's degree or two years with a PhD, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

• Have solid experience with mammalian cell culture processes, including bioreactor operations and scale-up.

• Have experience with late-stage process development, such as process characterization, scale-down models, or technology transfer.

• Can design studies, apply statistical methods, interpret complex data, and communicate scientifically sound conclusions.

• Have experience with process risk assessments and preparing clear scientific reports and technical documentation.

• Communicate effectively with clients and cross-functional colleagues and are fluent in written and spoken English.

Experience with JMP, DoE, AMBR250, DSMQ, FMECA, statistical equivalence testing, process modelling, or regulatory submissions will be an advantage. We recognize that candidates may bring different combinations of these skills and do not expect you to have experience with every method or technology listed.

You work independently, take responsibility for your commitments, and maintain high standards of scientific quality. You can structure your work and prioritize competing tasks, even when project requirements change.

When challenges arise, you approach them calmly and logically, communicate openly about progress and risks, and involve colleagues or your manager when support is need.

You are comfortable discussing scientific findings with clients, explaining the rationale behind your recommendations, and working with others to resolve challenges. You value mutual respect, open communication, and learning from colleagues.

**What We Offer

**At AGC Biologics, you will work on different client projects, helping prepare mammalian upstream processes for clinical and commercial manufacturing.

**We Offer

**

• The opportunity to lead late-stage upstream development studies and work on different scientific and process challenges.

• A multidisciplinary environment where scientific discussions, collaboration, and knowledge sharing are part of everyday work.

• A manager who gives you room to plan your work independently, values honest discussions, and is available when you need support.

• An initial mentoring arrangement to help you become familiar with our processes, systems, and ways of working.

• Access to our canteen arrangement, Employee Club, and employee discount opportunities.

**Interested?

**If you are motivated by combining scientific expertise, project responsibility, and client collaboration, we would like to hear from you.

Please submit your application and CV through our recruitment system. Applications will be reviewed continuously, and we reserve the right to close the job posting once we have found the right candidate.

**Expected Start Date: February 1, 2027

****Who We Are

**AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market.

Drive meaningful impact across the life sciences industry.

As our next Senior Consultant, you will contribute to solving meaningful challenges across the life sciences industry. We offer specialised management consulting services, working with top-tier life sciences companies as well as biotech startups — locally and globally. From strategy development to hands-on implementation, we support our clients were impact matters most.

About the role

We are looking for highly motivated and ambitious Senior Consultant who can contribute across a broad spectrum of projects — including implementation, optimization, and ongoing consulting for the commercial area (SFE,CRM). The role is open to candidates with either a technical background or a business consulting mindset, as long as you bring curiosity, structure, and a collaborative spirit.

You will work closely with cross-functional teams, helping clients translate business goals into scalable, system-supported solutions.

Your responsibilities include:

• Lead workstreams or small teams on client projects, ensuring high-quality delivery and stakeholder alignment.

• Conduct process assessments and define future-state operating models across commercial functions.

• Translate business needs into system requirements and support end-to-end implementation of platforms.

• Facilitate workshops, gather requirements, and manage documentation (e.g., project plans, RAID logs).

• Support IT and commercial strategy definition, including CRM optimization and system integration.

• Drive change management activities, including training design, stakeholder engagement, and adoption planning.

• Act as a trusted advisor to clients, bringing structure, insight, and industry best practices.

• Engage in Sales processes by taking part in RfP responses and delivering presentations.

You bring:

• 5+ years of experience ideally in project-based roles within consulting or the life sciences sector implementing solutions for the commercial area.

• Required consulting and hands-on experience in Salesforce, Veeva, and other CRM systems (certifications in Salesforce and Veeva will be a plus). Technical understanding is a plus, especially for projects involving IT collaboration.

• Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.

• Strong communication skills, both verbal and written in English.

• Ability to create compelling presentations and confidently present to diverse audiences.

• Proactive mindset with a “can-do” attitude and eagerness to learn.

• Comfortable working in agile teams and remote environments.

• Project Management and Agile methodologies experience (certifications on Agile, PMP... will be a plus).

• Experience facilitating workshops and driving client expectations into sustainable solutions.

• Ability to influence senior stakeholders and manage change at scale.

• It will be a plus if you have these additional capabilities:

• Experience working in global or regulated industries (e.g., pharma, finance).

• Prior consulting experience — especially in top-tier consulting firms — is valued but not required.

• Exposure to enterprise platform rollouts or system integration projects.

• Experience with project management and collaboration tools such as Jira, Confluence, or similar platforms.

• Experience contributing to Salesforce Effectiveness initiatives, including CRM usage optimization, sales process alignment, and support for user adoption strategies.

• Interest in emerging technologies and AI.

This position is offered in Denmark.

Who is BASE life science?

Founded in 2007, BASE life science is a business and technology consulting enterprise working exclusively in the life sciences industry.

With headquarters in Denmark and offices across Europe and the United States, we support clients globally. We work closely with our customers to identify, develop, and implement initiatives that drive growth, efficiency, and meaningful change. Through partnerships with leading solution providers such as Veeva, Salesforce, IQVIA, Benchling, and MediSpend, we help our clients unlock the full potential of modern technologies.

Why join BASE Life Science?

At BASE, you work on meaningful, complex challenges at the intersection of technology, science, and business. We trust our people with real responsibility and support them in turning ambition into impact.

You will be part of a collaborative, high‑performing environment where:

• Ambition is encouraged through ownership and continuous learning

• Execution matters — we focus on delivering solutions that work in practice

• Team spirit and trust guide collaboration across roles, countries, and disciplines

• Openness means your ideas are heard, you are challenged constructively, and supported as you grow

Alongside this, we offer:

• Support for health and wellbeing, covering physical, mental, and social needs

• Flexible ways of working, built on trust, autonomy, and balance

• Ongoing learning and professional development throughout your career

• A modern work setup, with the tools and equipment needed to do great work

• Recognition of performance and impact, linked to contribution and results

• The opportunity to work on challenges that make a meaningful difference for patients and healthcare systems worldwide

Explore our work, values, and people at www.baselifescience.com

Interested?

If you find this position intriguing, don't delay—submit your application in English at your earliest convenience. We are continuously reviewing and assessing all incoming candidates and eagerly await your application.

Department: Sales EMEA

Location: Copenhagen

**Description

**Factbird helps manufacturers improve performance with an AI-enabled, plug-and-play manufacturing intelligence suite. Real-time visibility on the shop floor. Connected operations. Data that actually turns into improvement, not just reports.

We’re expanding our Northern European sales team in Copenhagen and looking for a Business Development Representative to help us keep building momentum and opening doors in a market where we already have a solid presence. You’ll work from our Copenhagen office and support our Danish and Swedish markets, so we’re looking for someone fluent in both languages.

This is a great role for someone early in their sales career who wants more than a script to follow: someone who wants to help shape our outbound approach, sharpen their craft with modern prospecting tools, and sell something that makes a real difference on the factory floor.

**About the Role

**As a BDR at Factbird, you won’t just be executing outreach. You’ll be helping sharpen the playbook for how we generate pipeline in Denmark and Sweden. That means a mix of hands-on prospecting and real input into strategy: which accounts to target, which messages resonate, and which channels and tools actually move the needle.

You’ll spend your time identifying the right accounts, reaching the right people, testing what works, and turning interest into qualified meetings and sales opportunities.

This is a phone-first role. Phone calls remain your primary tool, but you’ll also run structured multi-channel campaigns across email and LinkedIn, and use AI-powered prospecting tools to work smarter, not just harder.

**Key Responsibilities

**We’re looking for someone who understands that outbound success comes from a combination of activity, discipline, messaging, and follow-through. This role is aligned with market expectations for outbound development work, including periods where 100-200 call attempts per day may be required, depending on territory focus, campaign goals, and lead quality.

What you'll do

• Build qualified pipeline through targeted outbound prospecting into manufacturing and industrial accounts across Denmark and Sweden

• Respond to inbound leads, qualify interest, and convert it into meetings

• Research target accounts to understand business context, likely pain points, and buying relevance

• Identify the right decision-makers and stakeholders within target organizations

• Book discovery meetings for the Account Management team and create qualified opportunities

• Maintain strong prospect data quality and keep HubSpot accurate and up to date

• Track your performance against KPIs and stay disciplined about activity and follow-up

• Work closely with the Account Management and Marketing teams to sharpen targeting, messaging, and handoff quality

• Bring insights from prospect conversations back to the team: what’s resonating, what isn’t

**How we'll measure success

**KPIs will be defined with your manager, but here's what we're tracking:

• Sales-qualified leads generated

• Discovery meetings booked and completed

• Conversion from leads to qualified opportunities

• Outreach volume, especially calls

• Inbound lead response time

• CRM discipline and data quality

This role is for someone who wants to see a direct line between their daily work, the strategies they help build, and commercial growth.

**About you

**You want to build a career in sales, and you’re ready for a role where you get real ownership, not just a list of calls to make. You’re comfortable in an outbound environment, curious about tools and experimentation, and motivated by the opportunity to improve fast.

We’re looking for someone with:

• 1-3 years of experience as an SDR in a B2B SaaS environment

• Fluency in Danish and Swedish, and strong English

• A strong interest in pipeline generation and outbound prospecting

• Comfort working in a phone-first sales development role

• The ability to succeed in a high-activity environment, including periods of 100-200 calls per day

• Curiosity about the manufacturing world and interest in learning how manufacturers operate

• Strong follow-through and personal ownership

• Experience working in a CRM, ideally HubSpot

• Hunger for a long-term career in sales

If you’re excited by building pipelines, learning fast, and helping bring modern software into manufacturing environments, we’d love to hear from you.

**Why Factbird?

**People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

• Flexible working hours — we trust you to manage your time

• Competitive salary — compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact

• Internet reimbursement — stay connected wherever you choose to work from

• Thoughtful, human onboarding — step-by-step support from day one

• Individual Development Plan conversations — bi-yearly career development aligned to your ambitions

• Company-wide kickoffs & team days — we come together regularly across teams and regions

• A global, inclusive culture — diverse backgrounds and perspectives, actively celebrated

**Join Us

**If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit, feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Apply directly or reach out with questions to our Global Talent Acquisition & People Operations Lead, Khristel, at khma@factbird.com.

Please note that applications will be reviewed after November 20th.

_At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

DevOps Engineer - Keep the Engine Room Running at RiskPoint

On behalf of RiskPoint, we are looking for a curious and methodical DevOps Engineer to join their growing IT-team. If you are building your DevOps skills and would rather see your work running in production than parked in a slide deck, this could be your next career opportunity.

About RiskPoint:

RiskPoint Group is a fast-growing global Managing General Underwriter (MGU), providing specialist insurance solutions across multiple lines of business in close partnership with leading insurance companies. With more than 325 employees in 18 locations, RiskPoint combines deep underwriting expertise with in-house claims handling and strong business support.

As a DevOps Engineer at RiskPoint, you will become part of a cross-functional global IT-organisation within Finance and Operations, spanning development, architecture, data, infrastructure, and business partnering. RiskPoint is targeting a doubling of the business over the next three years, powered by a digital and AI portfolio built in-house: rating engines on one shared core, AI pipelines that read and route transaction documents, and renewal workbenches redesigned from actual underwriter voice notes. All of it depends on builds, deployments, and environments that simply work.

RiskPoint operates in an agile, collaborative environment with strong cross-border cooperation. Several systems are mid-migration at any given moment, and changes ship across Cyber, Directors and Officers (D&O), Transaction Risk, and Property in parallel. If that sounds chaotic, it is the fun kind. With a flat structure and a culture built on trust and responsibility, RiskPoint offers real impact, ownership, and room to grow.

About the Position:

As a DevOps Engineer at RiskPoint, you will help the teams deliver software reliably by supporting delivery pipelines, cloud environments in Microsoft Azure, and day-to-day automation. You will work close to the engine room of the digital and AI portfolio, helping keep the platforms behind rating engines, AI pipelines, and business applications stable, secure, and repeatable.

This is a role for someone who is building their DevOps skills. You will start with well-defined tasks and build confidence through pairing, code reviews, and guided troubleshooting with experienced colleagues. The focus is on contribution and learning rather than architecture or leadership, and there is real room to grow.

The position is based onsite at RiskPoint's Copenhagen office, and you will collaborate closely with developers, architects, operations and security colleagues, as well as external vendors.

Your key responsibilities will include but not be limited to:

• 
Support CI/CD pipelines by maintaining build, test, and deployment steps, investigating failures, and validating changes before release

• 
Assist with cloud and infrastructure configuration in Microsoft Azure, including routine maintenance and environment checks

• 
Make small, reviewed Infrastructure as Code changes, for example in Terraform, and write or adapt scripts that automate repeatable tasks

• 
Support Kubernetes-based deployments and Helm-based configuration to keep runtime environments stable and consistent

• 
Monitor dashboards, alerts, and logs, troubleshoot methodically, record findings, and escalate when needed

• 
Follow good security and access practice, including least privilege, safe secret handling, and prompt reporting of potential risks

• 
Maintain clear setup guides and runbooks

• 
Use AI tools to understand unfamiliar scripts, draft documentation, and speed up troubleshooting, always with review before production

Please note that applicants must currently reside in Denmark and hold a valid work and residence permit. Fluency in both written and spoken Danish and English is required.

Your Profile - A Great Match for RiskPoint:

For this position, we are looking for a structured, analytical, and pragmatic DevOps Engineer who enjoys working a problem through until it is solved, and documenting it so that nobody has to solve it twice.

You have a relevant education within Computer Science, Information Technology, or a similar discipline, though equivalent practical experience counts just as much as the diploma.

The role carries an underlying expectation: you use AI to build your own methodology, not just RiskPoint's products, and reach for it by default.

To succeed in this role, you should bring:

• 
Foundational knowledge of Git, including commits, branches, and pull requests

• 
An understanding of basic cloud concepts, operating systems, and networking

• 
The ability to read and adapt simple scripts in PowerShell, Bash, Python, or similar

• 
A methodical approach to troubleshooting, with the patience to work a problem through and record what you find

• 
Clear communication and a willingness to ask questions, learn from feedback, and document solutions

• 
An interest in agile delivery environments using Jira and GitHub as core engineering tools

You are humble and comfortable collaborating with both technical and non-technical colleagues, and you see feedback as fuel rather than criticism.

Although not required, RiskPoint would prefer candidates who have:

• 
Some exposure to Microsoft Azure, Azure DevOps, or GitHub Actions

• 
Some exposure to Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or Bicep

• 
Some exposure to containers such as Docker, and to Kubernetes or Helm

• 
Personal projects or coursework where you have built, deployed, or automated something end to end

If you are as comfortable discussing a pricing factor or a data schema as you are discussing sprint velocity, this could be your next career opportunity.

RiskPoint Group is a fast-growing global Managing General Underwriter (MGU), providing specialist insurance solutions across multiple lines of business in close partnership with leading insurance companies. With more than 325 employees in 18 locations, RiskPoint combines deep underwriting expertise with in-house claims handling and strong business support.

About the Position:

As a Product Owner for Rating Engines at RiskPoint, you will own the most data-intensive systems in the portfolio: the rating engines that price the risk, and the portfolio management tooling that gives underwriting leadership a real-time view of exposure, concentration, and performance across lines. This is not a roadmap of screens and forms. It is a roadmap of models, calibration logic, and data pipelines.

You will decide what is a Quick Win, what is a Strategic Bet, and what is a Wildcard worth a flutter, with a meaningful share of the ideas coming from data science and actuarial, not just underwriting. You roll out changes through a staged, evidence-led ramp rather than a big bang, and you know when a change touches live pricing and needs a careful hand.

RiskPoint is not hiring to maintain what exists, but to build what doubles the business. That means real ownership, a genuine mandate from leadership, and work that ships in weeks, not quarters, and runs in production rather than gathering dust as a pilot.

The position is based onsite at RiskPoint's Copenhagen office.

Your key responsibilities will include but not be limited to:

• 
Own the backlog and roadmap for the rating engines, including the shared pricing core, product-specific rating logic, and the calibration and versioning discipline that keeps a live pricing system trustworthy

• 
Own the backlog and roadmap for portfolio management tooling, including exposure aggregation, concentration risk, and loss ratio trending

• 
Prioritise using the 5is framework (Inventory, Ideate, Incubate, Implementation, Iteration), scoring ideas against evidence, sponsorship, and sized benefit before they are resourced

• 
Write requirements and acceptance criteria that hold up against a data pipeline and a model, not just a user interface

• 
Partner with data science and engineers on the underlying models, understanding what drives a price change well enough to defend it to underwriting

• 
Define what good looks like for a new pricing factor or model version, and know when it needs data science or actuarial sign-off

• 
Sequence model and feature rollouts across regions and lines of business, from shadow mode through partial live to full automation, based on measured accuracy and error rates

• 
Use AI tools yourself to query rating engine output logs, run quick data explorations, and draft technical requirements against a schema

• 
Own stakeholder communication end to end, briefing leadership honestly about both what has shipped and what is still shaky

Please note that applicants must currently reside in Denmark and hold a valid work and residence permit. Fluency in both written and spoken Danish and English is required.

Your Profile - A Great Match for RiskPoint:

For this position, we are looking for a structured, analytical, and pragmatic Product Owner who can sit between underwriters, actuaries, data scientists, and leadership, and speak each of their languages fluently.

You have 3-5 years of experience as a Product Owner or Product Manager, ideally owning a data-heavy or model-backed product such as a pricing engine, risk scoring, or an analytics platform.

The role carries an underlying expectation: you use AI to build your own methodology, not just RiskPoint's products, and reach for it by default.

To succeed in this role, you should bring:

• 
Comfort reading model outputs and asking sharp, informed questions about them, even without a data science background yourself

• 
Genuine fluency in agile ceremonies, and the judgement to know when process should flex to reality

• 
A sharp instinct for MVP scoping: what ships now, and what waits

• 
Practical, hands-on use of AI tools in your own workflow for requirements, data exploration, or documentation

• 
Strong stakeholder management skills and the ability to adjust your register to underwriters, actuaries, data scientists, and leadership

You are humble, and honest about uncertainty rather than dressing it up.

Although not required, RiskPoint would prefer candidates who have:

• Familiarity with how rating or pricing logic works in insurance or a comparable regulated, model-driven industry

jobs.description:
**Your impact begins here

**You will support in building the experimental foundation of a new interdisciplinary team in Global Research, established to generate and validate innovative therapeutic concepts in cardiometabolic disease and healthspan. As one of two Advanced Laboratory Technicians in In vivo Research, you will turn scientific questions into well-executed rodent studies and shape the team’s capabilities from the start. Your work helps bring new projects into the early discovery pipeline.

**What You Will Bring

**You are a trained laboratory technician, hold a relevant technical qualification, or bring equivalent practical experience.

• Strong hands-on experience in rodent research, including mouse and rat handling, dosing and sampling.

• Relevant training and authorisation for the animal procedures you will undertake, as applicable.

• A careful, organised approach to experimental work, documentation and data quality.

• The ability to work independently within agreed study plans and to coordinate with colleagues.

• Curiosity, practical problem-solving skills and an interest in learning new methods.

• Confidence in sharing observations, suggesting improvements and asking questions.

• The ability to communicate and document your work in English.

**Useful, But Not Essential

**

• Metabolic phenotyping, including food intake, body composition, glucose regulation or indirect calorimetry.

• Behavioural testing and neuroscience-related experimental methods.

• Rodent surgery and postoperative care.

• Tissue dissection, sample processing and ex vivo methods.

• In vitro assays supporting pharmacological or mechanistic studies.

• Establishing new laboratory methods or workflows.

You are not expected to bring experience in every technique. We welcome complementary profiles.

**What You Will Do

**Working closely with scientists and fellow laboratory technicians, you will contribute to studies that test new ideas and help set up how the team works in the lab. More specifically, you will:

• Plan, coordinate and perform mouse and rat pharmacology experiments, including dosing, observations, sampling and relevant physiological measurements.

• Perform metabolic phenotyping and contribute to behavioural studies, according to your expertise and training.

• Collect and process biological samples for ex vivo and laboratory analyses.

• Contribute to developing, optimising and troubleshooting experimental methods.

• Record, quality-check and organise experimental data, and flag observations that may affect interpretation or later studies.

• Bring practical expertise to study planning and to discussions of results.

• Help establish laboratory workflows, maintain equipment and coordinate materials and study activities, working to relevant procedures, animal welfare requirements and the principles of replacement, reduction and refinement.

Depending on your experience, you may also contribute to rodent surgery, specialised neuroscience methods or in vitro assays. Training will support the introduction of additional techniques.

**Who You Will Work With

**You will join a new interdisciplinary team in Global Research, part of Research & Development, working alongside scientists and laboratory colleagues with expertise in physiology, pharmacology, neuroscience and molecular innovation. Scientific and technical colleagues plan experiments together, deliver them together and interpret the observations together, so your view counts at every step. The team is headed by Christoffer Clemmensen.

You will also work with animal facility staff and laboratory specialists across the organisation.

**What You Can Expect Here

**You will help shape the experimental practices of a new team. Your technical judgement, observations and suggestions will be valued as part of the research process, and you will be trusted to work independently within agreed study plans.

Salary and Benefits**:** The Annual Base Salary ranges from 499,600.00 to 734,400.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. Benefits package also include a free choice account of currently 10% and 4% holiday allowance.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn scientific questions into well-executed studies and help build a new team’s lab from the ground up, apply for the Advanced Laboratory Technician – In vivo Research role by 22 November 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so apply as soon as you can.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

About the job Our purpose is to bring hope to life by enabling life-changing therapies for patients around the globe, creating a healthier and happier tomorrow. Our mission is to work side by side with our customers to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market. Are you a detail-oriented student who thrives on organizing information and supporting technical teams? Do you want hands-on experience in a fast-paced biopharmaceutical environment? Then join AGC Biologics as a Student Assistant in our Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team—where your work helps map and optimize our cutting-edge production facilities. At AGC Biologics, you’ll join a fast-growing biopharmaceutical company where quality, collaboration, and continuous improvement are part of everyday life. As Student Assistant in our Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team, you’ll play a key role in organizing information, analysing data, mapping our facilities, and supporting the team while they keep our production and utility systems running at top performance—supporting life-changing treatments for patients worldwide. About the Team The Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team in Engineering comprises of dedicated technicians, engineers, and coordinators with a strong focus on personal development, collaboration, and high professional standards. We operate with a flat structure where every contribution matters and decisions are made collaboratively. Our culture emphasizes ownership, continuous learning, and mutual support. We work closely together to maintain critical production equipment and promote a safe, innovative, and engaging work environment. About the Role As a Student Assistant in our Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team, you will be primarily responsible for: Support the day-to-day operations of the Equipment Maintenance and Calibration team (e.g., data entry, document control, coordinating small tasks) Lead the facility mapping initiative by collecting and verifying the Process and Instrumentation Drawings (PIDs), building layouts, electrical and utility drawings, service and maintenance agreements, and spare-parts inventories, etc. Consolidate information into our CMMS or a central digital repository, ensuring accuracy and ease of access for the team Assist in updating and maintaining equipment records, location tags, and asset lists Collaborate with technicians and engineers to clarify technical details and resolve gaps in documentation Contribute ideas for improving our documentation processes and data workflows Analyze facility data (drawings, service agreements, spare-parts inventories, etc.) to identify gaps, validate completeness and produce clear, data-driven reports that guide maintenance planning and process improvements. This role offers flexible hours to accommodate your study schedule and the possibility of a longer-term internship if desired. Your Qualifications We are looking for a candidate who: Is enrolled in a relevant technical or engineering program (e.g., mechanical, electrical, industrial engineering, etc.), preferably in the first year of your education Demonstrates strong organizational skills and a keen eye for detail Has excellent communication skills in English and preferably Danish, both written and verbal Is proficient with Microsoft Office (Excel, Visio, Power BI) and eager to learn CMMS tools or CAD basics Is self-motivated, reliable, and able to work independently as well as part of a team What We Offer This role will give you insight into the design and operation of biopharmaceutical production facilities, as well as how the various departments collaborate to deliver life-changing therapies. On top of that, we offer the following: Meaningful tasks that directly support our maintenance operations and facility improvements Mentoring from experienced technicians and engineers Flexible scheduling to balance work and studies A collaborative, supportive work culture in a leading biopharmaceutical company How to Apply Applications are screened on an ongoing basis. You do not need to attach a cover letter to your application, but please include a few sentences about your motivation for applying to this position. If this sounds like the right challenge for you, we’d love to hear from you. Don’t hesitate to apply – even if you don’t meet every single requirement. The right mindset matters just as much. If we see a potential match, one of our recruiters will contact you to discuss your application. If you have any questions, please contact Sameer Ahmed (Senior Manager, Equipment Maintenance and Calibration) on +45 50106391 or on LinkedIn. Who We Are AGC Biologics is a global Contract Development and Manufacturing Organization with a strong presence in Denmark. From our Søborg site, we develop and manufacture life‑changing advanced biologics for some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies. Together with our team members across Europe, the U.S., and Japan, we deliver development and manufacturing of mammalian and microbial-based therapeutic proteins, plasmid DNA (pDNA), messenger RNA (mRNA), viral vectors, and genetically engineered cells therapies. Across our global network, we are united by one mission: To work side by side with our customers in order to improve patients’ lives by bringing new biopharmaceuticals to market. AGC Biologics is Your Friendly CDMO Expert – dedicated partners with the expertise and commitment to support our customers and teams. We work with some of the world’s most innovative pharmaceutical companies to develop and manufacture their life-changing drug products. If you’re motivated by meaningful impact and ready to join our journey, we invite you to explore our current opportunities!

SOUNDBOKS is an innovative tech company and aspiring lifestyle brand. You may have seen us at a music festival, street party, or your friend’s celebration (think: private events combining festival-grade sound with beat-enhancing lights) where special moments are turned into memories. We create the loudest, most durable, and arguably coolest Bluetooth speakers and audio reactive lights on the market.

At SOUNDBOKS, trust and community go hand in hand. People are encouraged to take ownership of their work while knowing they have the support of the team behind them. Voices are heard, ideas are welcomed, and collaboration is what pushes us forward.

This is more than a job - it’s a community where people care about each other, celebrate together, and share the energy of creating something meaningful. Life at SOUNDBOKS is bold, fast, and full of passion - for the product, for the mission, and for showing up as your true self. With 70 team members, this is a place where you can do your best work and truly belong.

ROLE ACOUSTIC ENGINEER

TEAM PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

HOURS FULL TIME

LOCATION COPENHAGEN, DENMARK

START DATE OCTOBER 2026 or ASAP

The Product Development team at SOUNDBOKS is the group responsible for the exciting product journey, taking every step of the development process toward and into mass production. In it’s heartbeat you’ll find collaborative and self-driven team members with a large cross-discipline understanding tied to ownership. They are there to make a difference - for the products, the team and the SOUNDBOKS customers as a whole.

Every SOUNDBOKS starts with a great idea - but turning it into a speaker that can survive a festival, run for hours, and sound incredible takes a lot of engineering. As the Acoustic Engineer, you'll be taking charge of the acoustic development that helps bring those products to life.

Okay, let’s make things a little more concrete. Here’s what we expect your daily life to look like:

**Concept & Prototype Development

**

• You'll select and design acoustic components based on product and market requirements.

• You'll define initial enclosure concepts.

• You'll build and evaluate proof-of-concept prototypes to validate acoustic concepts.

• You'll collaborate with Mechanical Engineering during the early product development phase to mature acoustic concepts.

**Simulation & Validation

**

• You'll perform acoustic simulations with a focus on sound pressure level (SPL), sound quality, and system efficiency.

• You'll validate simulation results through physical testing.

• You'll collaborate with suppliers to refine acoustic components based on simulation and test results.

**Driver Specification & Verification

**

• You'll own the technical specification of loudspeaker drivers towards suppliers.

• You'll define driver specifications and tolerances.

• You'll support manufacturing verification with suppliers.

• You'll participate in the acoustic verification of the final product towards mass production.

• You'll collaborate with the Audio team on audio signal handling, including crossovers, compressors, and limiters.

**In order to become a success in this role, we believe that your profile should be aligned with the bullets listed below. However, we acknowledge that success can take many forms, so please do apply even if you don’t tick all the boxes.

**

• You have proven experience designing and simulating loudspeakers, including transducer design and specification, enclosure design, and acoustic measurements.

• You hold a BSc or higher in Audio, Acoustics, Mechanical, or a related engineering discipline.

• You've done loudspeaker simulation and measurements, and use both to validate and refine your designs.

• You've worked with loudspeaker development from concept through verification and ideally have experience collaborating with external manufacturing partners.

• Familiarity with crossover design, FEM simulations, or failure analysis is an advantage.

• Ideally you also have experience building physical speaker mock-ups or collaborating with large-scale loudspeaker manufacturing partners.

• You work independently, take ownership of your area, and enjoy collaborating closely with engineers across disciplines.

• You're curious, creative, and constantly looking for ways to improve acoustic performance.

• You're drawn to what SOUNDBOKS is building and are excited to be a part of the journey!

Intrigued? At SOUNDBOKS you’ll find yourself a part of a community. We realize that growth is a process and we don’t expect you to go through it alone. Actually, we guarantee that you won’t have to. We work together in order to work smarter, we inspire each other to be better, and we never forget that every member of the team is responsible for our success.

So, if you’re tired of all of the noise in the job market, we’d love to hear from you. This may be the coolest job you ever have!

jobs.occupation: Design for Value & Cost Engineer – from concept to competitive edge, GN Hearing, Ballerup
jobs.description:
Are you ready to apply your engineering, project leadership and sourcing expertise to the world of product development and manufacturing? Join us as Senior Project Manager in Design for Value (DfV) and impact the way we design, develop, and manufacture products at GN Hearing in Ballerup.

The team you will be part of:

Based at our global HQ, located in Ballerup, Denmark, you will join the Design for Value team in Global Manufacturing & Operations, reporting directly to Director René Bergqvist.

In this role, you will collaborate with internal and external stakeholders worldwide, ensuring value and cost are managed effectively and optimized in our products from the early concept phase through to mass production.

Your contribution is appreciated and you will:

• Optimize products by supporting the organization with cost / value analysis in our products, modules, platforms and architecture

• Investigate and motivate for cost-effective design and manufacturability, e.g. via mapping of value / cost opportunities related to roadmap, product, and design options

• Manage cost targets and running estimate for ramp up in development projects

• Facilitate and support project sourcing activities including availability reviews, supplier selection, RFQs, and negotiations

• Support building positive business cases together with R&D & Product Marketing

• Facilitate and conduct project reviews related to Design for Value, Cost and Manufacturing

• Follow up and guard the cost in product development by working with R&D on their suggested specification, manufacturing or material selection

You will also work on introducing new technologies and innovations during product development and play a key role in approving targets and results before critical milestones are passed.

You will also support key cross-functional projects that are part of strategic initiatives (“must-win battles”) with significant value or savings impact from an Operations and Sourcing perspective.

To perform well in the role, we imagine that you - besides having a technical mindset and a good business understanding - have:

• A degree or similar within engineering, preferably within electronics

• Experience within platform and product development, supplier sourcing or cost/value optimization in a R&D environment are positive differentiators

• Good at solving both technical and commercial issues

• General understanding of manufacturing processes and industrialization

• Experience with LEAN, Design for Value/Cost, or supplier sourcing in Asia, are positive differentiators

• Presentation, negotiation, and communication skills in English, both written and spoken

In addition, you have an engaging personality and possess facilitation skills, enabling you to build networks and engage stakeholders. You also possess solid analytical and problem-solving abilities, which you use to identify issues and propose effective solutions.

You are, furthermore, steadfast and enjoy working in a multicultural, changing environment. You take initiative and, most importantly, follow through on the initiatives you start.

We offer:

• A unique opportunity to grow and gain experience across both engineering and business

• A supportive and dynamic work environment where you can learn to navigate change with confidence

• Opportunities for professional and personal growth in a top-tier global high-tech company.

• The chance to contribute meaningfully to GN

• An international and collaborative workplace

We encourage you to apply

We highly value a mindset, motivation, and energy, that align with our core values, to not only ensure your growth, but for your team and the wider GN organization as well.

We are focused on an inclusive recruitment process

All applicants will receive equal consideration for employment. As such, we encourage you to submit your CV without a photo to ensure an equal and fair application process.

Should you have any special requirements for the Interview please let the hiring manager know upon accepting invitation to interview.

How to apply?

Use the ‘APPLY’ link no later than 25 November 2026. Applications are assessed on a continuous basis, so don’t wait to send yours.

On a time crunch? Feel free to only submit your up-to-date CV including a few sentences outlining your motivation for applying – quick and easy.

Join us in bringing people closer

GN brings people closer through our leading intelligent hearing, inspired by people and driven by innovation, we deliver technology that enhances the senses of hearing and sight. We help people with hearing loss overcome real-life challenges, improve communication and collaboration for businesses and provide great experiences for audio and gaming enthusiasts.

GN has entered into a definitive agreement for the sale of GN’s Hearing business to Amplifon S.p.A. to create a global leader in audiology. For GN Group, this creates an opportunity to expand our position in the large audio and video peripherals markets. Read more about the announcement here.

We hope you will join us on this journey and look forward to receiving your application.

Are you passionate about delivering great customer experiences and solving technical challenges?

At Trackman, we are looking for a service-minded and technically curious Customer Service Specialist to join our Business Tools Support team.

In this role, you will be a key point of contact for customers worldwide, helping them get the most out of our innovative sports technology. From troubleshooting technical issues to guiding new customers through onboarding, you will play an important role in delivering a seamless and professional customer experience.

You will join an international and collaborative environment where customer satisfaction, problem-solving, and continuous improvement are at the heart of what we do.

Meet the Team

You will join our Business Tools Support team in EMEA, a collaborative team of six supporting the digital platforms and services used by Trackman venues worldwide, including Booking & Payments, the Trackman Portal, and venue onboarding.

Working closely with customers, Sales, Product, and Development, the team resolves technical and operational challenges and continuously improves our solutions. You will have the opportunity to develop your technical knowledge, support international customers, and contribute to delivering excellent customer experiences.

What will you be doing?

As a Customer Service Specialist, you will combine customer service with hands-on technical support. Your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Customer Support: Respond to customer inquiries via phone and email, providing professional, friendly, and efficient assistance.

• 
Technical Troubleshooting: Identify, diagnose, and resolve technical issues related to Trackman products, software, and connected devices.

• 
Customer Onboarding: Guide new customers through product setup, configuration, and usage, ensuring they feel confident using our solutions.

• 
Product Guidance: Educate customers on product features, updates, and best practices to help them get the most out of Trackman technology.

• 
Case Management: Handle multiple support requests, prioritize effectively, and maintain accurate documentation in our support system.

• 
Follow-up & Customer Satisfaction: Proactively follow up on customer cases to ensure successful resolutions and positive experiences.

• 
Collaboration & Improvement: Work closely with colleagues and other departments to resolve complex issues, share knowledge, and continuously improve our support processes.

What are we looking for?

We are looking for someone who enjoys helping people, has a natural interest in technology, and thrives in a dynamic, international environment.

Ideally, you bring:

• 
Previous experience in customer service, technical support, or a similar customer-facing role, preferably within a technology-related industry.

• 
Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken.

• 
A customer-focused mindset with excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting abilities.

• 
Confidence working with Windows operating systems, computers, and common technical devices such as monitors, projectors, and mobile devices.

• 
Experience with ticketing or customer support systems, preferably Zendesk.

• 
The ability to manage multiple requests, prioritize tasks, and maintain a high level of service in a busy environment.

• 
A proactive, structured, and collaborative approach to your work.

It would be an advantage if you also have:

• 
An interest in sports, particularly golf, baseball, or sports technology.

• 
Basic knowledge of networking and connectivity.

• 
Experience with remote troubleshooting and technical diagnostics.

• 
Additional education or training in IT, customer service, or a related field.

• 
Flexibility to work weekends when required.

Most importantly, you are curious, eager to learn, and motivated by making a difference for customers.

What can we offer?

At Trackman, you will become part of an international technology company where innovation, sports, and passion come together.

You will have the opportunity to work with advanced sports technology used by athletes, coaches, and organizations worldwide, alongside talented and dedicated colleagues.

We offer a collaborative working environment, opportunities to develop your technical and customer service skills, and a culture where initiative, ownership, and new ideas are valued.

The Office

We are located at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the state-of-art building we have designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness center, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and be mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

Where innovation happens

At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

Share our Passion!

If you are excited about combining technology, customer service, and sports, we would love to hear from you!

For additional information about the position, please contact Jade Palphreyman, Business Tools Lead EMEA, at japa@trackman.com.

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**The Senior Manager, Biostatistics acts as a biostatistician supporting the clinical development of compounds as compound lead, primarily up until proof of concept, and/or as trial responsible statistician.

**Responsibilities

**Compound/Indication Level

• Act as lead and main point of contact related to Statistics for designated compound/indication

• Follow scientific and technical progress within the field of biostatistics in drug development and advise of new methodologies that may support innovation and improve efficiencies

• Engage with regulatory authorities on compound/indication level discussions

• Acts as a role model

• Ensures consistency of statistical methods and data handling across trials

• Ensures all compound/indication related work and information is shared between biostatisticians involved in the compound and with the vendor

• Supports compound responsible programmer in developing an integrated database specification

**CDT Member

**

• Responsible for giving statistical input to overall strategy and the synopsis development in the CDT

• Provide scientific advice to the CDT including design of trials, analyses and analyses requiring advanced statistical methodologies/techniques

• Represent the CDT/the company at regulatory meetings, during Key Opinion Leaders meetings, network and/or Partner meetings, as applicable

• Drive design and synopsis development together with relevant stakeholders

• Ensure transparent communication to relevant stakeholders from the CDT

• Ensure availability of integrated database(s), as needed, and planning and conduct of integrated analysis to support development decisions, submissions, and marketing needs

• Support development and communication in relation to communication strategy and/or scientific input to presentations, posters, and articles

Trial Level

• Represent Genmab during meetings/congresses and courses and perform professional networking

• Engage with regulatory authorities on trial level discussions

• Arranges/attends lessons learned to share learnings

• Represents Genmab during Key Opinion Leaders meetings

• Ensure biostatistician review of partner synopsis, protocols, statistical analysis plans, results meetings presentations and clinical trial reports

• Coordinate data transfers from/to business partners in collaboration with the programmer and the data manager, as applicable

**CTT Member

**

• Participate and represent Biostatistics

• Review and provide input to protocol and amendment development

• Perform vendor oversight according to applicable SOPs

• Give input to eCRF setup, edit checks, validation plan, protocol deviations classifications, DSUR, IB updates, tables, figures, and listings etc.

• Review assay validation reports, as applicable

• Perform exploratory analysis, ad hoc analyses, and modelling of data

• Review and approve randomization and stratification plans

• Perform UAT of Randomization part of the IRT system as applicable

• Ensure procedures for blinding are in place as applicable

• Support timely delivery of statistical deliverables

• Responsible for planning and conducting trial result meetings

• Review and approve the CSR

• Attend operational and steering committee meetings, as applicable

• Support regulatory submission/filing activities

**Requirements

**

• MS / PhD or equivalent in a statistical discipline

• 5+ years of experience in relevant area preferred or demonstrated capability

• Experience in statistical analysis, modelling and simulation and adaptive trial designs

• Experience in working with clinical trials

• Preferred experience with oncology clinical trials

• Proficient programming skills in statistical software’s, such as SAS

• Excellent oral and written communication skills

• Ability to work independently as well as in teams

• Confident, self-reliant, and a quick learner

• Proactive and open-minded

• Ability to prioritize and work in a fast-paced and changing environment

• Result and goal-oriented and committed to contributing to the overall success of Genmab

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$130,560.00---$195,840.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.
